The same holds for Y.

Therefore the expectation of X plus Y exists.
That expectation is finite.
It equals the sum of the two expectations.
This is the usual linearity property.
It does not require any special construction.
It also does not depend on independence.
It holds for all integrable random variables.
A discrete example cannot violate it.
The requested counterexample is therefore unavailable.
If one uses a nonstandard conditional series idea, the terminology changes.
Then a series may converge without absolute convergence.
But that is not the standard meaning of a finite expectation.
So the safe answer remains no.
